Learn Why The Bull Case For IBM Stock Could Change Following Quantum Computing Expansion
Mitch Lawler

IBM
MSFT
NVDA
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

International Business Machines recently announced a series of quantum and AI moves, including new Nighthawk processors, a Chicago Quantum System Two deployment, multiple co-design platforms with partners such as NVIDIA, AMD, Fermilab, and Oak Ridge, and an AI agent platform collaboration with Microsoft.

These projects point to IBM leaning heavily into capital-intensive, research-heavy quantum and enterprise AI infrastructure. This could influence long-term margins, required investment, and how its Software, Consulting, and Infrastructure segments work together in practice.

The next area of focus will be how IBM's existing hybrid cloud and AI investment narrative aligns with its quantum co-design initiatives with NVIDIA.

Spot 53 AI infrastructure stocks that, like IBM, are pouring resources into quantum-ready AI hardware and enterprise platforms before this buildout phase matures.

International Business Machines Investment Narrative Recap

To own International Business Machines, you need to believe its shift toward hybrid cloud, AI and now quantum-ready infrastructure can keep earnings and cash flow resilient while growth stays moderate. Recent quantum and AI partnerships, plus the new Nighthawk roadmap, keep that thesis focused on Software and Consulting execution rather than one-off hardware wins.

The immediate catalyst is how quickly IBM converts its reported generative AI book of business into higher margin Software revenue and stable free cash flow. The recent yen fixed-income deals look incremental. They tweak funding and interest costs but do not materially change the near term risk, which still centers on high debt and execution in AI.

The IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 and r3 announcements look most relevant to this buildout. They sit right where the story is heading, toward quantum-ready AI infrastructure that leans on IBM Quantum Platform, classical supercomputing tie-ins, and a growing ecosystem across partners like Oak Ridge and AMD.

For you as a shareholder, the key issue is how effectively IBM turns that technical roadmap into commercial Software and Consulting projects that support margins while also funding capital-intensive quantum work. Execution on this front will likely matter more to the catalyst than funding mechanics. At the same time, the existing high debt load still depends on consistent free cash flow to remain manageable.

On kapirey's numbers, the narrative reaches a fair value of US$256.08 by applying a discounted cash flow style framework that assumes IBM can compound revenue at 6.0% a year and eventually sustain an 18.0% profit margin on that higher sales base.

title: Chase Bank outage sparks issues for customers at several major US banks
detail:
Chase Bank outage sparks issues for customers at several major US banks
Brittney Donovan
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 3:53 PM CST 3 min read
MSFT
Trade MSFT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Customers at several major banks in the United States complained of issues Monday after a technical glitch at JPMorgan Chase apparently caused ripple effects throughout the financial system.

Thousands of Americans rushed to outage tracking website downdetector.com to report issues accessing Bank of America, Chase, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo services on Monday afternoon. The technical issues seemed to be centered around Chase customers and customers at other banks trying to transact with Chase, per the Associated Press.

Chase confirmed it was experiencing an issue but said it was not the result of a cyberattack.

"Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds," a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. "We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible."

An ATM machine displays a 'not working' screen at a Chase bank in Irving, Texas, Monday, Nov. 16, 2026 (AP Photo/LM Otero)

A photo showed an ATM in Texas displaying an error message and Chase customers across the U.S. reported receiving a message stating: "Some services aren't available. We're working on them. Please try back later."

A spokesman for U.S. Bank said its systems were unaffected, but "clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays."

Zelle allows customers to send funds almost instantly. The peer-to-peer system is owned by Arizona-based Early Warning Services, which is held by banks including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo.

A spokesman for Early Warning Services said the Zelle network was operating fully, noting, "An issue at the financial institutions may be delaying Zelle payments for some of their customers."

A woman unsuccessfully tries to use a drive-up ATM machine at a Chase bank in Irving, Texas, Monday, Nov. 16, 2026 (AP Photo/LM Otero)

A Zelle spokesperson added: "Zelle is operating as it should. Consumers use Zelle through participating banks and credit unions, which manage their accounts and hold their funds."

Tech issues top of mind for Americans

The issues affecting Chase and other banks followed a major Microsoft outage last week that lasted for about 20 hours. Services used by millions of people across the globe, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, went down, leaving people unable to work.

In addition to the Microsoft outage, the bank issues also come on the heels of a massive outage that triggered a nationwide ground stop for all US flights on Friday. Airports are still recovering from the blackout, which led to 14,000 flight cancellations on Friday and Saturday.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the outage was the result of upgrade work on the nation's aging air traffic control system. He told reporters that defense contractor L3Harris was working to replace a section of the system's old copper wire with new fiber wire, and that work somehow caused a system overload.

Duffy said officials were investigating whether contractor "incompetence" or a faulty router was the cause. The incident has raised questions about whether safeguards should have prevented the disruption.

title: Microsoft (MSFT) Is One of NVIDIA’s Biggest Customers, and a Growing Rival
detail:
Microsoft (MSFT) Is One of NVIDIA’s Biggest Customers, and a Growing Rival
Venkatesh Srinivasalu
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 3:30 PM CST 3 min read
MSFT
NVDA
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

We just published our list of the 10 Stocks to Buy Following Jensen Huang's Departure, and Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) rounds it out at number 10.

Microsoft (MSFT) Is One of NVIDIA's Biggest Customers, and a Growing Rival

For three years, the AI trade had one face. Now it has an interim CEO. On November 12, Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA's chief executive and board member, hours after nerves gripped investors awaiting the outcome of the board's crisis meeting. CFO Colette Kress is running the chipmaker on an interim basis while the board searches for a permanent successor. Analysts moved fast: Bernstein downgraded the stock to Market Perform and halved its target to $200, Baird cut it to Neutral, and Morgan Stanley dropped it from its Top Pick list.

The bigger question is cyclicality, not succession. At about 11x forward earnings, NVIDIA trades far below the S&P 500's roughly 19–20x, even after 106% revenue growth last quarter, a sign the market doubts those earnings will last. That is why money is spreading across the AI ecosystem: custom accelerators, the networking that ties clusters together, the clouds renting out compute, and the equipment that fills data halls.

Why Microsoft Made Our List

We built our list from U.S.-listed companies that sell alternatives to NVIDIA's products, from AI chips and networking to cloud services and data center equipment. To qualify, a company needed a market cap above $40 billion and Buy ratings from at least 70% of covering analysts. We then took the 10 largest and ranked them by median analyst upside.

Microsoft Corporation qualified because Azure rents AI capacity to customers regardless of which chips power it. With a market cap of $3.89 trillion, Buy ratings from 93% of 59 analysts, and a median price target of $635 against a November 13 close of $523.88, the stock offers 21.21% upside, which placed it 10th on our list.

Microsoft Corporation: An NVIDIA Alternative

Microsoft is one of NVIDIA's biggest customers, and it is turning into one of its quiet competitors. Azure sells AI capacity by the hour, and the customer renting it rarely cares whose chip sits underneath. That gives Microsoft room to fill its data centers with its own Maia accelerators and AMD's new Helios racks as well as NVIDIA hardware.

The demand behind that strategy is visible in the fiscal Q1 report from October 28. Azure grew 48%, revenue of $92.3 billion beat estimates, and commercial remaining performance obligations jumped 73% to $677 billion. That is a backlog of contracted cloud demand Microsoft can route to whichever silicon gives it the best economics.

title: NVIDIA: The Most Important Earnings Chart This Week
detail:
NVIDIA: The Most Important Earnings Chart This Week
Tracey Ryniec
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 4:01 PM CST 2 min read
NVDA
PANW
MSFT
CSCO
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Earnings season continues to roll on and we're going to start hearing from a lot of the retailers. But there is also a smattering of technology companies that will report including Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and NVIDIA Corp. NVDA.

Even under normal circumstances, NVIDIA's earnings are always a "must-watch" event. But this week will mark the first earnings report without founder Jensen Huang. NVIDIA's conference call will be led by Colette Kress, NVIDIA's new Interim CEO. Prior to being appointed to that position, she was the CFO for the last 13 years.

Before joining NVIDIA, she had long-term stops in the finance groups at Microsoft and Cisco.

NVIDIA is an Earnings All-Star

On Nov 17, 2026, NVIDIA will report its fiscal third quarter 2027 results. NVIDIA has a great earnings surprise track record. It has only missed on earnings three times in the last five years.

But since the AI Revolution began in 2023, NVIDIA has only missed once. That miss was in 2025 when it missed by just 3.8%.

I'm expecting it to keep its earnings surprise track record this quarter. It will likely beat again. After all, the quarter had ended before the former CEO, Jensen Huang, resigned.

What Comes Next for NVIDIA?

Earnings are expected to jump 91.5% this quarter to $2.49. NVIDIA made just $1.30 per share a year ago.

But what happens from here?

For fiscal 2027, earnings are expected to rise 94.6% to $9.28 compared to just $4.77 last year.

Will NVIDIA provide guidance for the fiscal fourth quarter 2027 and full year 2027?

NVIDIA is Cheap Now

Shares of NVIDIA have slid 27% in the last month. But that means it's gotten more attractive on a valuation basis.

NVIDIA has traded with a price-to-earnings (P/E) around 40 for years. A P/E ratio over 30 is considered to be expensive. But currently, it's trading at just 17x. That's the cheapest it has traded in years.

It's price-to-sales (P/S) ratio has also plunged to just 12.95. Sure, a P/S ratio above 10 means an investor is paying a lot for the sales. But NVIDIA's P/S ratio was above 20 for most of the last 3 years.

Historically speaking, NVIDIA is on sale.

NVIDIA is a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) stock.

title: Days after Microsoft and the FAA went dark, Chase and Wells Fargo customers can’t get to their money
detail:
Days after Microsoft and the FAA went dark, Chase and Wells Fargo customers can’t get to their money
Catherina Gioino
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 2:35 PM CST 3 min read
WFC
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

If you had trouble logging into your bank's website on Monday, you're not alone. JPMorgan Chase customers spent much of the day unable to log in or move money, with the bank saying the outage spread from it's website and app to some branches and to outside apps that connect to Chase accounts. Wells Fargo also confirmed problems with its online banking, and customers at other large banks reported trouble.

Reports started Monday morning and climbed quickly. Downdetector logged nearly 4,500 Chase reports shortly after 1:30 p.m., most of them about website logins. By 2:22 p.m., the count had passed 20,000.

"Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds," a Chase spokesperson told Fortune. "We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible."

Customers described a wider disruption than that statement suggests. Comments on Downdetector mentioned problems with ATMs and in-person systems as well as online banking and Zelle. Some customers opening the Chase app got a message reading, "Some services aren't available."

The problems also reached apps outside the bank. Plaid, which links bank accounts to payment, investing and budgeting apps, said its own network was working normally but that it was seeing connection problems with Chase accounts. Customers trying to link or refresh a Chase account through another app may have gotten errors as a result.

Downdetector listed Chase, Wells Fargo, Capital One and Bank of America among the banks with spikes in outage reports, along with U.S. Bank, Truist and Zelle. By 2 p.m. Eastern, Bank of America saw about 2,000 with U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo seeing about 1,000 each.

It's also affecting local branches. On the subreddit r/TalesFromYourBank, one person wrote: "I'm at work and haven't been able to take a single client." Three others corroborated to their bank phone systems being down.

Bank of America and U.S. Bank had not explained their customers' problems as of Monday afternoon. Downdetector counts user complaints, not confirmed outages, and it was not clear whether the Chase and Wells Fargo failures shared a cause.

The outages follow several other technology failures in recent days. Microsoft restored service on Saturday after a global outage took down Outlook and Teams, and said a technical problem, not a cyberattack or AI, was the cause. No bank has tied Monday's problems to the Microsoft outage.

Meanwhile, a Federal Aviation Administration comminications problem grounded flights across the country on Friday, with service not fully restored until Monday. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed an upgrade from copper wire to fiber-optic cables at one location that caused routers across the air traffic control system to be flooded with more than 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. Because it disrupted some radar feeds, the FAA ordered the ground stop to ensure safety. It was lifted about four hours later.
